sources.title: Fourier transforms of positive definite kernels and the Riemann xi-Function
sources.inspection: Selected statements and the full-line normalization in (3.11)–(3.14) checked. Pólya's convex-kernel criterion and the associated-kernel characterization are used as classical tools. Section 4.6 switches to a half-line transform; this review derives constants from the full-line statement instead of copying (4.7).
sources.inspection_provenance: Inherited selected-passage inspection; not a new full-paper audit.
sources.relevance: Sections 2 and 5: separate the convex primitive criterion from positive definiteness of associated kernels. The latter is stronger than pointwise positivity.

sources.title: The Riemann Hypothesis and the Turan Inequalities
sources.inspection: Selected primary pages inspected as rendered images because the PDF is scanned. The integrated kernel is K(t)=integral from t to infinity of Phi(sqrt(u)) du. It is not the manuscript's psi_theta. The proof treats moment indices at least two analytically and the first separately; the full 21-page proof was not audited.
sources.inspection_provenance: Inherited selected-passage inspection; not a new full-paper audit.
sources.relevance: Section 4: the principal precedent for integrating first and then proving a stronger shape inequality. K is explicitly distinguished from p and G.

sources.title: Orthogonal polynomial expansions for the Riemann xi function
sources.version: arXiv:1902.06330v3, 5 May 2019; related published article Acta Arithmetica 200 (2021), 259–329
checked_passages: Section 3.1, (3.1)–(3.5), Theorem 3.1; introduction; Section 4.2 discovered but excluded from the requested primitive-centered review.
sources.inspection: Version-specific section numbers refer to v3, not the later journal article. Coefficient positivity and compact convergence were checked. This is an adjacent basis-change approach, not a direct theorem about the manuscript's primitive. No assertion that real-rooted basis functions force real-rooted partial sums.
sources.inspection_provenance: Inherited selected-passage inspection; not a new full-paper audit.
sources.relevance: Section 6: a possible change of basis with positive coefficients. No real-rootedness conclusion is imported from coefficient signs alone.

sources.title: Probability laws related to the Jacobi theta and Riemann zeta functions, and Brownian excursions
sources.version: Bulletin of the AMS 38(4), 435–465; version read arXiv:math/9912170v1, 21 December 1999
sources.inspection: Selected transformations and probability identities checked. The HTML shows an apparent recompilation date; bibliographic provenance uses the submission record and publication date. Positivity and infinite divisibility apply to the specified variables/transforms, not automatically to the logarithmic variable relevant to xi zeros.
sources.inspection_provenance: Inherited selected-passage inspection; not a new full-paper audit.
sources.relevance: Section 6: retain the precise random variable and transform when translating theta identities into probabilistic language.

sources.title: Zeros of combinations of the Riemann Xi-function and the confluent hypergeometric function on bounded vertical shifts
checked_passages: Introduction, (1.1)–(1.6); Theorem 2; Section 2 boundary calculation at z=0, (2.5)–(2.10) and Lemma 6.
sources.inspection: Direct link between the undifferentiated theta expression and Hardy's zero argument checked. The review only uses the ordinary z=0 circular approach to the theta boundary, with its decay independently explained; it does not import the paper's more general all-route boundary assertion or audit its hypergeometric extension.
sources.inspection_provenance: Inherited selected-passage inspection; not a new full-paper audit.
sources.relevance: Section 3: the principal modern source for Hardy’s use of the same undifferentiated theta expression. Hardy’s original 1914 paper was not separately inspected; attribution is through this account.

sources.title: Remarks on Polya's theorem on characteristic functions
sources.version: Institute of Statistical Mathematics, Cooperative Research Report 175, 133–145; author PDF dated 13 December 2004
checked_passages: Discovery: indexed first-page Theorems 1.1–1.2 and author bibliography.
sources.inspection: Full primary PDF retrieval failed (web timeout/502 and verified-certificate download failure). Retained as a reading lead, not an imported theorem source. The convex criterion used in the review is checked directly in Csordas Theorem 3.4. Pólya's 1949 original is bibliographically identified there but was not separately read.

sources.title: On some positivity properties of the Riemann Xi function
sources.version: Author-hosted preprint v2, 29 October 2026; separate site/version numbering
sources.inspection: Selected claims and finite verified-zero dependence checked, not independently audited. The reciprocal-transform densities are different from the primitive in this investigation. The reported PF256 and finite-interval generalized Laguerre results are not treated as a new global theta sign bound.
sources.inspection_provenance: Inherited selected-passage inspection; not a new full-paper audit.
sources.relevance: Section 6 background only: preserve the finite verified-zero and finite-order qualifications. It is not an input to the opening arguments.

sources.title: Jensen polynomials for the Riemann zeta function and other sequences
sources.inspection: Fixed-degree eventual hyperbolicity and its Hermite limit checked. The sufficiently large shift depends on degree. This does not establish the all-degrees/all-shifts RH criterion and is not a uniform statement about physical heat time.
sources.inspection_provenance: Inherited selected-passage inspection; not a new full-paper audit.
sources.relevance: Section 4: a subsequent coefficient-based result with a fixed-degree quantifier, distinct from a global all-degrees conclusion.
